name: Japan
notes: House of Representatives: 289 single-member constituencies (first-past-the-post) + 176 PR seats in 11 regional blocs (D'Hondt, no threshold). Baseline: the 8 February 2026 snap election (LDP 316 seats, a two-thirds majority). District baselines: full candidate shares for all 289 districts scraped from the ja.wikipedia district articles (all sums exactly 100), with the top-two candidates relabelled to the en-wiki caucus parties (the CRA alliance's candidates often ran as ballot independents, e.g. Hokkaido 1st; Fukui 2nd's winner is a ballot independent en-wiki lists under the LDP caucus). Polls: the voting-intention (proportional vote) tables - decided-voter shares, the same measure as the vote model. District winners are projected by plurality; the swing is anchored on the 2026 national PR result. Backtest (2026, T-0): vote-share MAE 2.62, seat MAE 8.89, leader correct - the residual is dominated by the real system's list-exhaustion forfeiture reallocation (2026: LDP 82 by D'Hondt -> 67 final), which depends on nomination strategies and is not modelled. Geometry: the Commons 2024 constituency map (data-name labels; Akita unlabeled, Wakayama-2 typo and the Shimane-1 inset leader line handled; 2022 reapportionment cuts included). Party names follow the 2026 realignment: the Centrist Reform Alliance became the Democratic Reform Party (DRP, 民主改革の会, split 17 Sep 2026) and Reiwa Shinsengumi became the Party of Life. Next election: by February 2030.
